Revealed-preference size effect (acted-on median $700 vs ignored $360) evaporated under a within-month control: July acted $705 vs ignored $700, August $325 vs $300 -- size does not predict whether the user acts. The apparent effect was pure time-confounding (8/9 acted-on rows are July, 33/37 ignored rows are August). Do not re-derive or auto-apply a sizing correction from pooled acted-vs-ignored size comparisons; always split by period first.

cmd_journal prices tickers only from the current run's holdings.json, so an exited ticker can never be priced and its journal entry stays verdict:open forever. This creates survivorship bias in every bucket hit rate -- entries that fail to score are disproportionately the ones that went wrong enough to get stopped out. Fix (Phase 1): give cmd_journal an injected --prices-json like cmd_score/cmd_stops already have.

The tier-cliff bug: CONVICTION_TIERS' step-function pct field, looked up directly, meant two candidates one point apart on either side of a tier boundary (e.g. score 44 vs 46 across the 45pt low/medium line) got a 2x size difference for a 1-point difference in conviction. WDC reached the highest evidence tier (primary verification) and its size did not move at all because it stayed on the low side of the 45pt line. Fixed same-day by splitting tier LABEL (still discrete, for display) from tier PCT (now piecewise-linear interpolation via TIER_PCT_ANCHORS).

A proposal's 'action' field must be a verb+ticker sentence ('Sell ASML'), never a bare direction word ('SELL') -- the dashboard renders it verbatim as the row label. A hand-written batch of 7 proposals set action to a bare direction on 2026-08-29 and the dashboard showed 'SELL SELL'/'BUY BUY'/'TRIM TRIM'; the user caught it, not the system. Fix: never hand-write a proposal dict. Use 'smith_math.py add-proposal --proposals-json <specs>', which builds action FROM ticker+direction so the bug class can't recur, and validate_proposals_schema now makes this a hard validate defect if it ever does.

Never hand-type a run's full narrative into ledger.csv's 'notes' cell -- it is exactly the medium a fact drifts in. A nonexistent '8% drawdown warn line' (policy.json's real drawdown_warn_pct is 15) was typed once into a ~4,000-char notes blob and effectively copied forward across four consecutive runs before anyone checked it against policy.json. Fix: use 'smith_math.py append-ledger --summary <short, max 300 chars> --briefing-file <full narrative path>' -- the short cell is what validate_policy_narrative_drift actually checks, so a repeat is now catchable same-run.
